(beside lines 3 to 6), and note "Imitationis exempla." (beside lines 10 to 11). Running head at top right. Page number at top left. Nothing printed below the text except the catchword-like "II. main_text.p: qui reprehendunt alios, q; qui reprehen-duntur, vitam atq; mores confideret. lib.Materiæ responsionũ ad epist. expostulatorias.10.epist.34.35. Sunt autem responsionum eiuscemodi res & materiæ Ciceronis in epist.familiar.variæ. Responsio ad expo-stulationē de infrequentia & raritate litera-rarum.lib.2.epist.1.li.7.epist.13.li.12. epist.18.lib.15.epist.17. De non prœstitiis officiis, li.7.epist.27.De mora in repub.defenden-Imitationis exempla.da li.10.ep.8.De patrocinio & defensione improborū ac seditiosorū. lib.10. epist.31, 34.35.Nos exercitij gratia.lib.2.epi.1.imi-tari ex parte conabimur, in qua Curioni sese Cicero purgat: à quo ob literarū raritate accusatus & reprehensus fuerat.Nam & hodie fieri illud crebrò solet, ut propter silentiū diuturnū accusationes atq; expostulationes cū amicis instituantur.Partes epistolæ illius tres sunt.Exordiū significatione facti doloris ex accusatione amici perceptī.Excusatio & purgatio ἀρνήσει negatione partim, partim μετάστασει remotione facta. Præcisio & reiectio excusationis plixioris pollicitatio officij in scribendo. Quę imitado effingere poterimus hoc modo.

p.i: I. Etsi doleo, ob literarum me raritatem atq; infrequentiam accusari, tamen non tam hoc mihi graue molestumq; extitit, quàm gratū cognoscere, memoriam adhuc te mei tenere.

page.notes: Printed "II. Idq;" starts the next paragraph and continues on the next page. Lines 26 to 29 are set in italic. Greek words (ἀρνήσει, μετάστασει) are copied as printed. The printed "pli-xioris" is kept as "plixioris" because the hyphenated word is not clearly a continuation. The word "imitado" is copied as printed and is doubtful.
